articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Plasmonic Waveguide Based Wideband Terahertz Band-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A planar terahertz bandpass filter has been designed by analyzing the dispersion characteristics of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP). This design took advantage of the low-pass properties of SSPP and the high-pass attributes of SIW to achieve a wideband filter. In this design, the passband effectively covers a 3 dB frequency range of 0.3 THz to 0.7 THz while maintaining return losses consistently below -12.5 dB. The simulated insertion loss(IL) is 1.17 dB around the center frequency. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed filters exhibit sharp rejection out-of-band, possess a compact layout, and deliver a strong filtering response. These outcomes serve as compelling evidence of the filters' practical feasibility.

articleTitle: Effect of CeMgO2 ETL Parameter on CZTS Photovoltaic Cell Efficiency Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The electron transport layer (ETL) film materials were critical in the CZTS photovoltaic (PV) cell, which required excellent electron capture and a low minority carrier loss in ETL films. The high-minimization of minority carrier loss and high capture of ultraviolet (UV) photon-based ETL or buffer layer materials-based CZTS PV cells have been limited to development till now. Therefore, several researchers are investigating the high UV light-absorbing ETL materials for the making of efficient CZTS PV cells. In this paper, we model and analyze the proposed CZTS PV cell with the incorporation of novel wide energy bandgap and high UV light-capturing Mg-CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ETL materials. By placing the investigational constraints of each layer material to AFORS-HET, we first match the energy band alignment between Mg-CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CZTS layers and optimize the thickness and doping density. After optimization, the proposed device produced better performance in terms of η = 26.95%, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> =29.38 mA/cm2, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> =1089 mV, and FF = 84.28% compared to the existing device.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of SPR based PCF Using Scale-Down Approach for Potential Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The present study proposed a photonic crystal fiber based plasmonic sensor using scale down approach. Sensor structure is designed and studied numerically using Finite Element Method based COMSOL Multiphysics software. Gold film is used as active plasmonic material. Detail study shows excellent sensing parameters of high sensitivity and high figure of merit representing good specificity and stability. Proposed sensor is one of the potential candidates to be applicable in various sensing applications in food, chemical and biomedical industries.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Analysis of SLIPT Over Visible Light Gamma-Gamma Distributed Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is a widely investigated technique wherein energy harvesting (EH) occurs from ambient radio frequency signals (RF). With the rapid developments in Li-Fi, simultaneous light information and power transfer (SLIPT) become a significant and safe alternative for energy harvesting. In this work, we consider the line of sight (LoS) SLIPT communication link over gamma-gamma distributed visible light channels. For it, we develop an insightful statistical analysis of harvested energy. Specifically, we derive a closed form upper bound for average energy harvested. We present plots based on the numerical results and obtain useful observations. The analysis we present in this paper serves as a useful theoretical benchmark for multi-SLIPT EH-VLC models.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: Simultaneous light information and power transfer

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Dual-Side Polished SPR Based PCF Sensor for Blood Compositions Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A dual-side polished photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensor based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) with semi-arc micro openings is presented in this work for diagnosis of different blood compositions such as water, plasma, white blood cells (WBCs), hemoglobin (HB) and red blood cells (RBCs). In order to generate plasmons and monitor changes in the RIs of the sensing medium, gold (Au) is coated on a polished flat fibre surface as a plasmonic material. Different blood compositions cause distinct loss peaks at varying resonance wavelength when exposed as a sensing medium to the sensor. The shifting of the resonance wavelength is utilized to determine the wavelength sensitivity of the proposed sensor for distinct blood componsitios. Thus, the optimum wavelength sensitivity is achieved for hemoglobin-RBCs as 6500 nm/RIU which is considerably finer than those in the relevant state of the art and is simple to fabricate.

articleTitle: A Study of the Duty Cycle Dependence on the Intensity of Diffracted Orders of a Computer Generated Hologram
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The study of variation of intensity of diffracted orders of a hologram or diffraction grating with duty cycle (DC) is presented in this work. The intensity of various diffracted orders can be changed or controlled effectively by modifying the duty cycle which in turn will help in the studies involving higher diffracted orders. It is found that as the duty cycle decreases, the intensity of higher diffracted order increases. For DC=51.61%, the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order diffracted spot is absent. On the other hand for DC=25.00%, the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order diffracted spot is present.

articleTitle: Raman Scattering in a Silicon Photonic Nanocavity Operating at $1.1 \mu \mathrm{m}$
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The spontaneous Raman scattering spectra of a silicon photonic nanocavity operating in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.1-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> band are measured and compared with those of a nanocavity operating in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> band. We experimentally confirm that both nanocavities have similar quality factors (about 34,000) and find that the efficiency for Raman scattering in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.1-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> -band nanocavity is 5.4 times higher.

articleTitle: Optical readout of electronic spin state of nitrogen-vacancy center in nanodiamonds at room-temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The color centers in diamonds are promising candidates in the context of quantum information science, quantum computation, and spin-based quantum sensors due to their exceptional spin-dependent emission properties. The manipulation and the optical readout of the spin state is measured using a spectroscopic technique known as the Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR). Here, we discuss the indigenous development of an ODMR setup to manipulate and measure the spin state of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. The study involves the confocal mapping of NV centers to measure the spin state by applying a micro-wave field. The spin state control appears as a dip in the measured emission intensity as a function of micro-wave frequency.

articleTitle: Catadioptric Dual-FOV High Definition SWIR Imaging Sensor Optics for Security Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper delineates front end catadioptric dual FOV optical design for SWIR Imaging sensor. Discrete Zoom lens design is introduced for high definition uncooled InGaAs detector. The designed system for effective focal length 400mm operates at f/5 and for effective focal length 900mm operates at f/ll for fixed aperture. Relay system designing is also incorporated along with catadioptric architecture to make the system more compact. The optical design as well as performance parameter analysis in terms of the amount of flux collected by the optics and resolution achieved by the optics is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Nanomaterial Coated Side Polished Fiber for Early Diagnosis of Cardiovascular Disease by Label-free Sensing of Troponin Biomarker
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we report a high sensitive biosensor to prognosis of CVD. Further, Troponins is identified as diagnostic biomarker to detect the early diagnonis of CVD. We have proposed a high sensitive and label-free lossy mode resonance (LMR) based biosensor. To the best of authors' knowledge, this is the first report on fiber optic biosensor for detecting Troponins T (cTnT). Besides, the proposed biosensor detects the cTnT concentration from 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{g}/\text{mL}$</tex>. The proposed optical biosensor consist of a nanomaterial coated side polished fiber (SPF) to detect cTnT. The shift of the LMR have been noted as 41.74 nm for very low analyte concentrations due to features of SPF evanescent field interaction with cTnT. Thus, the proposed optical biosensor cater to the needs of the present demand to early diagnosis of CVD and reduce the risk factor associated with CVD disorders.

articleTitle: Vectorial light field encoding for asymmetric encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: An arbitrary vector light field encoding based asymmetric image encryption is proposed which contains two levels of security. Optical field has spatially varying non-uniform polarization due to which, it is called vector beam. Therefore, it is used in information security. In the proposed scheme, an input image is converted into stationary white noise using structured phase masks under the asymmetric approach. Thus obtained output is encoded with spatially varying polarized light which provides the stronger security and easy implementation. Original image is recovered computationally using experimentally recorded data. Recovered image verifies our scheme.

articleTitle: Optical Waveguide based Surface Plasmonic Resonance Biosensor for Early Detection of Human Teeth Cavity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a surface plasmonic resonance (SPR) based biosensors using MXene and MoWS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> materials deposited on gold grated aluminium (Au) metal for the early detection of human dental cavity disease. The numerical analysis of biosensors are performed to measure the sensitivity for various cavity thickness, by filling it with erythrosine. Further, the proposed planar-optical SPR sensor design exhibits a maximum linear sensitivity of 608.6 nm /RIU with respect to a changes in refractive index (RI). The highest sensitivity of the wave-guide based biosensor exhibits at a wavelength of 700 nm. Furthermore, the proposed biosensor is realized for the first time with the gold, chalcogenide material MoWS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and MXene in order to improve the bio-compatibility with dental layers for cavity detection. Finally, the proposed SPR based wave-guide sensor is a good candidate for oral care applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Low-Index Contrast Integrated Optofluidic Bimodal Waveguide Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we numerically study and assess the performance of a low-index contrast integrated bimodal waveg-uide (LIBiMW) sensor. The sensor is designed and simulated using the finite-difference time-domain method. The highest sensitivity was a 3.9% change in the normalized intensity for a refractive index change of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\triangle \mathrm{n}=0.0001$</tex> units. This study will aid in the optimization of the designs for the fabrication of integrated optofluidic bimodal waveguide sensors.

articleTitle: Design of discretely tunable Optical Delay Line on 45 nm SOI GF Fotonix Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: An integrated tunable delay line circuit based on Mach-Zehnder interferometers is presented on 45 nm Silicon- on-insulator GF Fotonix platform. Different waveguide lengths are studied to quantify the optical delay. Switching algorithm to tune the optical path for measurement of the delay is also presented. Experimental results show ~ 15 ps of delay for 1 mm long waveguide which matches with our simulation data of ~ 13 ps. The statistical data for the extracted group index across various sites and wafers is also presented. This circuit can be further be used for photonic signal processing by varying both the waveguide length and the optical input power.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Octagonal Cladding Photonic Crystal Fiber for Chemical Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this study, an octagonal-shaped liquid-infiltrated photonic crystal fiber (PCF) has been proposed for liquid sensing such as water and ethanol. The finite element method (FEM) based COMSOL Multiphysics software has been used for the analysis of the performance of the sensor. The PCF sensor is designed in such a way that it contains a hollow central circular core surrounded by five layers of octagonal cladding. The simulation was performed to obtain the best results in terms of relative sensitivity, confinement loss, power fraction, and effective mode index through numerical analysis. The relative sensitivities of water and ethanol were obtained relatively high at a lower operating optical signal, which were 95.344 % and 96.9 %, respectively. Also, the low confinement loss for these analytes was reported. The confinement loss for the studied PCF, were calculated to be 2.58 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> dB/m and 4.50 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> dB/m for water and ethanol, respectively. The proposed PCF can be fabricated easily for industrial use.

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum LSTM Based Diagnosing Localization and Characterization of Fiber Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this research work, a Hybrid Quantum Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) model is proposed for diagnosing two different occurrences namely, localization and characterization of optical fiber faults. On examining the simulation results, it reveals that the training and testing losses of the proposed Hybrid quantum LSTM, converged at the minimum epochs with low loss, produce superior performance and use less computation time than the classical LSTM for event localization and characterization of optical fiber faults.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Photonic Logic Gates with Organic Chromophore Molecules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Ultrafast reverse saturable absorption has been analyzed in detail in chromophore-based borondipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) derivatives with femtosecond (fs) laser pulses at 800 nm and 850 nm. The effect of pulse intensity, pulse-width, thickness, concentration, nonlinear absorption coefficients and laser pulse shaping on transmittance has been studied and optimized for the all-optical switching in recently discovered BODIPY derivatives, 1,7-Diphenyl-3,5-bis(9,9-dimethyl-9H-fluoren-2-yl)-boron-diuoride-azadipyrromethene (ZL-61) and 1,7-Diphenyl-3,5-bis(4-(1,2,2-triphenylvinyl) phenyl)-boron-diuoride azadipyrromethene (ZL-22). The results have been used to design low-power and high-contrast all-optical fs NOT, universal NOR, and NAND logic gates. The ZL-61 at 800 nm and 850 nm results in enhanced contrast than ZL-22 and therefore, all-optical logic gates with ZL-61 have better percentage modulation. The excellent nonlinear optical properties of organic molecules and their derivatives have tremendous potential for ultrafast all-optical computing and ultrahigh bandwidth information processing.

articleTitle: Impact of Barrier on the Absorption Spectra of Size Distributed III-V Quantum Dot Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In a quantum dots (QD) ensemble, the dots suffer from size non-uniformity which is traditionally modelled by a Gaussian distribution. In such QD systems, each dot is separated from the other by a higher bandgap material commonly known as barrier. It is likely that the wave function corresponding to the quantized energy states of the dot may extend into the barrier matrix. Earlier analytical models for the absorption coefficient have largely neglected the effect of this extended wave function. In this work, we have proposed analytical expressions for the inter-band absorption coefficient and linewidth of a size deviated QD system, taking into account the effects of the extended wave function of the quantized states into the barrier region through modifications in the effective mass of electrons/holes.

articleTitle: IQ Imbalance Tolerant Probabilistically Shaped Signals with Adaptive Constellation Referencing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS) can achieve information capacity scaling, even at a lower symbol rate. However, higher-order PCS is susceptible to nonideal system operations like IQ imbalance. In this abstract, we demonstrate the transmission of transmitter IQ imbalance tolerant probabilistic shaped 64QAM signal by employing a joint equalizer with reference constellation adaptation. The equalizer performs the carrier phase recovery and simultaneously adapts the ideal constellation to tolerate the IQ imbalance. We numerically investigate the algorithm's efficacy for PCS-64QAM signal for a range of imbalance and entropy values.

articleTitle: Effect of Particularly Ordered InxGa(1-x)N Based Quantum Barriers in III-Nitride Laser Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, the significance of particularly ordered InGaN quantum barrier on the electro-optical performance of III-nitrides based laser diode has been proposed, which leads to performance enhancement with significantly diminished electron outflux, threshold current density and piezoelectric polarization, along-with enhanced Laser power and optical field distribution. The laser power of the modified structure gets a significant drift from 129 mW to 213 mW. The electron outflux has reduced by 96% and hole influx has increased by 28% in the modified structure. The measurements are carried out at injection current of 120 mA.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Map and Predict Urban Area Using Landsat-8 Optical and Infrared Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The present work is an outcome of application of machine learning methods to map the urban land cover followed by future prediction of the urban area. For this purpose, Landsat-8 satellite data has been used which consists of optical and infrared sensors for image generation. The role of optical data for the present study is obvious which is highlighted by the application of machine learning methods, viz., CART classifier, LSTM, KNN, LR and RF. The machine learning methods are used to analyze the changes in the urban area using images from 2013 to 2021 and to forecast the growth of the urban area for the years 2022-2025. The study reveals that the urban area has expanded at the cost of agricultural land and vegetation areas. The predicted area of various land cover classes for the year 2025 has been determined for which the results obtained are promising.

articleTitle: A Numerical Insight on Fiber Optical Parametric Amplification in Yb-Doped Photonic Crystal Fiber for Mid-IR Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Mid-IR sources are currently a lookout in many fields that aspires for wavelength conversion processes as direct generation of those wavelengths is quite arduous with conventional technologies. This work is a numerical enumeration of the fiber optical parametric amplification (FOPA) process in a photonic crystal fiber (PCF) with Yb doped core that employs the single pump scheme. To accomplish this a profound theoretical insight into parametric amplification processes in such doped fibers is systematically Investigated through this work. A parametric gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.7\times 10^{-11}W/n{m}$</tex> is achieved in this process.

articleTitle: Analysis of Microring Resonator with Fock State Wavepackets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, a microring resonator is analyzed with fock state wavepacket at the input port and vacuum state at the add port. Photon flux density which is an important parameter of interest in quantum optics is analyzed at different ports of the microring resonator. The analysis is carried out by considering a Gaussian wavepacket of a fock state. It is observed that the photon flux density at output ports of the microring resonator is a function of frequency of the input optical signal and the magnitude of the photon flux density increases for higher order fock states. The analysis carried out in this paper will be helpful in understanding the quantum fluctuations which are important in the design of integrated quantum devices and circuits based on microring resonator.

articleTitle: 476 nm Broadband Generation from a Small Core and High Numerical Aperture Silica-based Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this report, broadband generation from an in-house fabricated highly germanium-doped fiber (HGDF) has been studied. The HGDF fiber is fabricated in our laboratory by the well-known modified chemical vapour deposition (MCVD) process. To introduce higher nonlinearity, the core radius of the fiber is reduced by the traditional rod-in-tube method and consequently, the NA is increased by increasing the doping concentration of GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to maintain the light acceptance property. An erbium-doped passively mode-locked laser has been used to pump the fiber after amplification. The pump source is capable of delivering 750 fs pulses at a repetition rate of 25 MHz. It is observed that at maximum available pump power, 700 mW, 20 m of HGDF fiber generates a broadband spectrum covering the wavelength regime from 1500 nm to 2000 nm, exhibiting a 20-dB spectral width of 476.4 nm. The impact of varying pump power on the generated broadband has been explored. A comparative study of broadband generation between the HGDF and commercially available UHNA-4 fiber has been performed to analyze the efficiency of the HGDF. It is found that the same length of UHNA-4 fiber generates broadband of 253.5 nm only.

articleTitle: Two Dimensional MMI Based 1×2 Optical Switch Using Square Core Multimode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The switching characteristics of an MMI optical device based on a square core multimode fiber (SCMMF) are presented. We show that the switching operations can be accomplished by controlling the relative phase of the input fields. The structure is all fiber and, therefore, can be integrated into the existing fiber networks.

articleTitle: 20 Tb/s Signal Transmission Over 50 km Optical Link of 80 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ Clad Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We have developed a prototype 80 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> clad optical fiber complying with ITU-T G.657.A2 with the longest spool length of 50 km ever reported, to the best of our knowledge. We have achieved the micro-bend loss of ≤1.38 dB/km at 1550 nm. We also demonstrate the successful transmission of 20 Tb/s over a 50 km optical link employing 80 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> clad fiber with a pre- FEC BER of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 2\times 10^{-4}$</tex>, which matched <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> clad G.657.A2 fiber of the same link length.

articleTitle: Bi-Core Photonic Crystal Fiber Based Chemical Sensor in THz Frequency Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This study proposes a chemical sensor based on bi-core photonic crystal fiber (BC-PCF) in the terahertz (THz) frequency regime with a novel construction that has two solid cores separated apart by a vertical elliptical hole filled with various chemicals such as ethanol, benzene, and water. Because of the ability that BC-PCF has to transmit light across all wavelengths, the solid core architecture is chosen for this sensor. The proposed sensor is able to attain extraordinarily high sensitivity because of the unique arrangement of circular and elliptical holes, which offers a substantial advantage over existing structures. The principle on which the proposed chemical sensor operates involves the coupling of modes between the two fiber cores. The finite element method (FEM) based COMSOL Multiphysics software has been used to comprehensively analyse and simulate the sensor's performance. Remarkably, the sensor is able to achieve a high sensitivity of 725833.34 nm/RIU with a fiber length of 0.2 meter. The use of this BC-PCF chemical sensor in the industrial sector is mainly aimed at efficiently identifying and detecting toxic chemicals.

articleTitle: Hybrid Routing Algorithm for Flex-Grid Optical Networks with Adaptive Modulation Formats
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A K-Hybrid Paths (K-HP) based Routing, Mod-ulation and Spectrum Assignment (RMSA) algorithm is pro-posed for Elastic Optical Networks. Simulation experiments are performed on two realistic network topologies to test the algorithm's performance. Simulation results verify the proposed K-HP-RMSA algorithm offers lower connection blocking under low as well as high traffic load conditions when compared to benchmark K-Shortest Paths-RMSA and K-Disjoint Paths (K-DP)-RMSA algorithms. It also borrows the K-DP-RMSA algorithm's resilience without compromising spectrum efficiency.

articleTitle: Conversion Efficiency >20% of Cs2TiBr6 Solar Cell: A Numerical Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The numerical simulation and investigation of lead-free Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> perovskite based high efficiency solar cells (PSCs) is reported by using solar cell capacitance simulator-1D (SCAPS-1D). In the present work, the material optimization of different holes transport layer (HTL) and defect density of absorber layer are accomplished. The optimum thicknesses of HTL and absorber's defect density are obtained as 10 nm and as 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, respectively. Among various materials, for most suitable HTL is MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> while TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is taken as electron transport layer (ETL). Finally, the optimized structure for lead-free PSC consisting of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>/MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> results the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.33% with V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> of 1.45 V, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> of 15.38 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and FF is 91.01%. Thus, the lead-free inorganic Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> perovskite provides an exciting alternative for fabrication of high efficiency and environment friendly solar cells.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Control of Terahertz Plasmons in Epitaxial Graphene Nanoribbons
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate ultrafast control of Terahertz (THz) plasmons in epitaxial graphene nanoribbons fabricated on semi-insulating SiC substrate. We investigated THz conductivity response from nanoribbons in both near- and far field THz regime and under ultrafast optical illumination. Optically pumping the periodic arrays of graphene results in changes such as a red shift in plasmon resonance, as well as widening and weakening of the response, all due to the transient heating of carriers. Under varying optical fluence, the transient terahertz transmission changes nonlinearly with increasing optical pump fluence.

articleTitle: Computation of Spot Diagrams and Ray Tracing of Different Aberrated Beams Using Geometrical Exact Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Aberrations are imperfections in optical systems, particularly lenses, that cause deviations from ideal image formation. They signify inaccuracy in performance from the predictions made by the paraxial approximation within the lens or optical system. Therefore, the measurement of various aberrations within the lens or optical system is essential for image analysis. Here, we will incorporate the concept of spot diagrams which are the intersection coordinate points of rays in the image plane of the lens system. This paper presents our research employing the geometrical exact ray tracing method, a tool suited for computing spot diagrams of several common monochromatic aberrations. Furthermore, we apply the same method to gain insights into chromatic aberrations.

articleTitle: Effects of Central-Dip on the Waveguide Parameters of NZDSF G.655 Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present theoretical studies on the effects of central dip on the optical parameters of dispersion shifted fibers (G.655). Experiments were carried out to study the central dip effect on the fiber. It was found that central dip causes non-significant effect till index dip is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<{=}$</tex> 58%, while it starts to affect the optical parameters after that value.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Sized Lens Array on Polymer Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A shallow lens array with hexagonally arranged millimeter-sized features is fabricated on thin, transparent and flexible polymer layer. A rapid, single-step inexpensive technique is demonstrated for the fabrication using soft- imprint lithography method. The patterned polymer layer is planar on one side and has concave dimples on the other side. The individual features have a size of 2 mm and the array shows efficient focusing characteristics with focal length of 4.891 mm and numerical aperture of nearly 0.205. The optical property of the patterned surface is studied with a pixel-level analysis of the recorded spot size, and is presented as the validation of the lensing nature of the surface. The extremely simple method for making the millimeter lens array has yielded a thin surface which possesses the focusing effect with a short focal length and diverges at larger distances. It can serve as an ideal diverging lens for the small-sized light sources such as LED and OLED, as well as a portable lens for viewing small objects in inexpensive microscope designs.

articleTitle: Design of a 2D Photonic Crystal Bacterial Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This work explicitly works on the theoretical design of the bacterial biosensor on the photonic crystal periodic structure. The FDTD and PWE methods, respectively finite difference time domain and Plane wave expansion methods, are used to anticipate different optical properties and dispersion behavior. The sensor is entirely dependent on changes in the R.I (refractive index) of the different analytes. Bacterial pathogens are responsible for major contamination in the drinking water. The different bacterial pathogens including E.coli, Vibrio cholerae, and Shigellae flexneri are analyzed in this work. The wavelength range in which the sensor operates is 1560nm to 1563nm. The developed bacterial sensor has a maximum quality factor of 2603.2.33 with a good sensitivity of 23.59 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: Terahertz Self-Reference Method for Classification of Flammable Liquids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we outline the terahertz (THz) spectroscopic study of flammable liquids. Terahertz selfreference spectroscopy method is employed to generate spectra of flammable liquids in terahertz region. The fingerprint spectra of these liquids would provide a crucial information about the characterization of flammable liquids. We provide a report on the optical properties flammable liquids such as ethanol, methanol, acetone, toluene and water. The absorption coefficient and refractive index are studied in the spectral range between 0.1-1.5THz.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Dengue Virus Using GaSe and WS2 Mediated Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor With Ultrahigh Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This manuscript presents a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor with outstanding sensitivity for the early identification of the dengue virus. The structure of the sensor includes a BK7 prism, Copper (Cu) layer, Gallium selenide (GaSe), Tungsten disulphide (WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), and a sensing medium (SM) with blood components, has been carefully developed and optimized. Using the transfer matrix method and MATLAB, WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has been identified as an excellent biomolecular recognition element (BRE), leading to remarkable sensor performance. The highest sensitivity (S) and a resonance angle shift (∆θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">res.</inf>) attained by the proposed sensor are 303.28 (°/RIU) and 10° respectively during infected platelet detection. COMSOL Multiphysics modeling confirms the sensor's ability to generate the extreme electric field intensity of 1.68×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> (V/m) with a penetration depth (PD) of 153.24 nm. This unique combination of PD and improved performance parameters positions the proposed SPR biosensor as a promising tool for early-stage dengue virus detection.

articleTitle: Digitally Encoded Arbitrary Microwave Waveform Generation Assisted by Photonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Generation of digitally encoded arbitrary microwave waveforms assisted by photonics is presented. Integration of two Mach-Zehnder modulators and a phase-shifter in the proposed microwave photonic system forms an essential part of this study. Gaussian pulses in microwave domain of frequency 1 GHz representing the input binary data are modulated onto an optical signal of wavelength 1550 nm. Depending upon the length of the input bit stream, phase-shift introduced by the phase shifter, digitally encoded (logical AND, exclusive OR) arbitrary microwave waveforms are generated at the output of the photodetector.

articleTitle: Tailoring Co3O4@ZnO Nano Composite Coating for Acetone Detection Using Unclad Optical Fiber Sensor at Room Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The current work offers an extensive investigation of a novel Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@ZnO nanocomposite as a coating material on an unclad glass fiber for acetone gas detection. The study examines the gas-sensing properties of three distinct fiber configurations, such as F-CZ1, F-CZ3, and F-CZ5. These sensor's output power gradually decreased as acetone gas concentrations increased, highlighting their sensitivity to low gas concentrations. Investigations into the interactions of acetone gas molecules with the Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@ZnO nanocomposite coating have shown that surface modulation and variations in refractive index are key factors in the modification of light travelling through the fiber core. The target analyte, an acetone, interacts with this evanescent light, which serves precise acetone gas detection. Due to its higher ZnO content, F-CZ5 showed the highest sensitivity of 0.006 nW/ppb and the lowest limit of detection (LoD) 1050ppb. Notably, the proposed sensor functions at room temperature and has a quick response time of 20 seconds, making it suitable for real-time monitoring applications. The design and characterization of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>@ZnO nanocomposite-based fiber optic sensors for acetone gas detection are discussed in this study. The promising results provide opportunities for further research and development, with potential applications in areas ranging from environmental monitoring to medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Effect of Cross-Talk in an Astigmatic Defocus Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The Astigmatic Defocus Sensor is a device for measuring the focusing error or the amount of defocus present in a beam. Cross-talk is a very important parameter in defocus measurement as it affects the accuracy of the measurement. Therefore, it is very important to have a proper analysis of the cross-talk effect and explore ways to overcome it. In this paper, we present an analysis of the presence of cross-talk in an Astigmatic Defocus Sensor and a possible way to minimize it. We provide simulation results in support of the analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Resonance Phenomena in Nested Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Nested Ring Resonator (NRR) structures are very popular for filtering and sensing applications due to their double fano resonance characteristics. Like MRR, the output of NRR is also significantly determined by the linewidth and sharpness of their resonance. The ring resonator along with the nested ring is capable of generating electromagnetically induced transparency, electromagnetically induced absorption and Fano lineshapes. In this work, we present a comprehensive study of different resonant lineshapes of NRR, which can be utilised for a multitude of applications. Moreover, we can utilise these lineshapes for producing different filtering responses, like Notch, Comb and Bandpass, by including one more cavity.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact PN Phase Shifter Using Straininduced SiGe for High-Speed On-Chip Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: By altering the medium's refractive index, optical PN phase shifters have the ability to change the phase of light. For high-speed on-chip applications, a portable PN-based optical phase shifter is presented in this work. To enhance modulation effectiveness and the impacts of the free carrier plasma dispersion, the device makes use of silicon that has been doped with germanium. The suggested device has been examined using both the Gummed-Newton iteration approach and the quasi-vectorial finite difference method. For a 480 nm × 220 nm cross-section rib waveguide with 50 nm slab height, a phase shift of 63<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>/mm and a VL of 0. 57V.cm at 2V reverse bias have been recorded. The device's footprint is measured as 1.14 mm. High-speed on-chip interconnects for optical communication systems at 1550 nm are compatible with the suggested phase shifter.

articleTitle: Broadband Optical Amplification Via Parallel Operation of Erbium and Thulium Doped Fibers in S, C, and Near-L Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Hybrid optical amplifier operating in parallel configuration of Erbium and Thulium doped fibers (E/TDF) has been proposed for S, C, and near-L (SCnL, 1460 nm to 1580 nm) bands of the fiber-optic communication system. Parametric optimization on the pumping schemes with respective optical powers, amplifier length, doping radius with concentration, and input signal power to the EDFA and TDFA modules have been performed. An average gain>15 dB has been achieved for an amplification bandwidth of 120 nm with the hybrid parallel amplifier. Overall noise figure (NF)>3.1 dB, a flat band (FB) gain of 15.69 dB for 1460 nm to 1516 nm, and a gain flatness (GF) of 2.38 dB have been calculated as the merit parameters. Also, for the maximum gain band (MGB) of 1520 nm to 1564 nm, an average gain>26.13 dB with respective maximum value of 51.24 dB has been achieved. The effect of ion-ion clustering mechanism (IM) on the signal gain is also investigated and minimized to 0.5% and 5.48% for a FB and MGB region respectively.

articleTitle: Investigations on The Linear/Nonlinear Optical Properties of CsPbBr3 Perovskite Nanocrystals Incorporated PVK Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The linear as well as nonlinear optical properties of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals incorporated poly(vinyl carbazole) thin film is presented. The CsPbBr3 nanocrystals were synthesized via ultrasonication. The as-synthesized nanocrystals are found to exhibit excellent green photoluminescence with high quantum yield. The nonlinear optical studies are performed by means of single beam Z-scan method in which an Nd:YAG laser delivering 532 nm pulses of nanosecond duration is employed. From open Z-scan analysis of the perovskite thin film, two-photon absorption is identified as the mechanism behind the nonlinear absorption phenomena of film. The prominent two photon absorption of the studied nanocrystals could be useful for various nonlinear optical applications such as passive Q-switching, up conversion, optical limiting etc.

articleTitle: Gold Immobilized Highly Sensitive PCF Optical Biosensor for Cancer Cell Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This work delves into the exploration of a dual-side polished PCF biosensor leveraging surface plasmon resonance (SPR) for the purpose of detecting diverse cancer cell types including adrenal gland, skin, cervical, and blood cancers. The investigation involves liquid samples of both cancerous and healthy cell states, each characterized by their respective refractive indices (Rls), to facilitate detection. Upon application of the cancer-affected sample onto the sensor probe proposed herein, an absorption peak materializes at the resonance wavelength, distinct from the absorption peak observed in the healthy sample. This disparity in absorption peaks serves as the basis for sen-sitivity measurement. Consequently, the proposed cancer sensor yields sensitivities of 15714.28 nm/ RIU, 21428.57 nm/ RIU, 18333.33 nm/ RIU and 16500 nm/ RIU for adrenal gland, blood, cervical, and skin cancer cells respectively. These nu-merical outcomes underscore the substantial credibility of our suggested biosensor in effectively identifying cancer cell types.

articleTitle: Novel Method for Efficient Control of Human Heart with Light
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Low-power, high-fidelity, large volume, synchronized excitation and suppression of cardiac cells is a maj or challenge in cardiac optogenetics. Although newly discovered powerful opsins that include ChRmine, a marine opsin gene from rhodomonas lens have significantly improved the excitable tissue volume, it is important to study the effect of light attenuation. In the present study, a novel method of gradient opsin-expression has been presented for enhanced volume suppression and synchronized excitation in human ventricular cardiomyocytes using ChRmine. The delayed action potentials ~ 18.6 ms in deeper layers of the tissue can be synchronized using this novel method. Furthermore, the proposed method allows to suppress the same tissue depth~ 6.9 mm at lower expression level. It would be very useful for effective treatment of cardioversion and tachycardia, and for extending the scale of cardiac optogenetics.

articleTitle: ZnO Nanoflower Decorated Optical Fiber Sensor for pH Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this report, an intensity-modulated no-core fiber (NCF) based sensor is fabricated and experimentally demonstrated for the application of pH measurement. The sensing head NCF was covered with two different layers: one is zinc oxide nanoflowers (ZnO-NFs) and another is a smart hydrogel. Nanoflowers were grown by hydrothermal technique and the hydrogel was applied via dip coating process. Some material characterizations such as XRD, FESEM, EDS, and optical analysis have been performed to confirm the coating morphology, composition, and optical activities of the ZnO nanomaterial. The sensor obtained a high sensitivity of 1.92 μW/pH in the acidic and basic pH range of 4-10 units. Along with that, the typical response time of 9 seconds and acceptable stability were also found.

articleTitle: Gap Solitons in Noncentrosymmetric Photorefractive Crystals with Apodized Photonic Lattices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Optical spatial gap solitons are analyzed in conventional photorefractive media having the Pockels effect with an embedded Gaussian apodized photonic lattice. In order to determine the band structure of a photonic lattice, the Floquet Bloch theory is applied. The presence of photorefractive nonlinearity within the photonic band gap facilitates the generation of solitons. The determination of the soliton solutions is accomplished through the utilization of the paraxial Helmholtz equation in both band gaps. Different forms of soliton solutions are observed in each band gap, including multi-hump, double hump and single hump solutions. An examination is conducted on the properties of these solitons across the entire band gap.

articleTitle: Corneal Hydration Sensing Studies Based on Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy and Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) radiation based corneal hydration sensing has shown potential applications in the field of ophthalmology. THz radiation between 0.1- 3.0 show susceptibility towards the water molecule which has proven to be advantageous in detecting changes in the water concentration in ex-vivo tissues. We report the study of terahertz hydration sensing of ex-vivo human cornea tissue collected from eye bank and successfully recorded the variation in the strength of reflected THz signal with respect to change in hydration of cornea tissues. The refractive index and absorption parameter of cornea tissue were measured between 0.1 to 2.0THz.. In addition, we have developed an indigenous THz time and frequency domain imaging system to study the change of hydration dynamics across cornea tissue.

articleTitle: Optical Biosensor Using One Dimensional Photonic Crystal to Detect Urea Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we numerically study the performance of a one-dimensional photonic crystal-based biosensor for the first time to detect the concentration of urea. We report the dependence of output intensity and shift in transmitted wavelength on the concentrations of urea. (GaP/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>/urea solution/ (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> /GaP) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> / glass is the photonic crystal structure used as biosensor. The transmission spectral studies are done using Transfer Matrix Method. The modification in the defect mode's position is due to change in values of refractive index is used to sense urea. The sensor characteristics such as sensitivity, Figure of merit and Limit of detection are optimized by varying the defect layer thickness and number of bilayer periods. With this structure, a sample of urea can be detected with maximum sensitivity of 660nm/RIU, figure of merit of 584.07 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and limit of detection of 9.92*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>05 RIU. This proposed design of this sensor can be utilized for the instantaneous detection of abnormal concentrations of urea.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Optical Fiber Sensor for Humidity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The development of a highly sensitive optical fiber humidity sensor for Relative humidity measurement (RH) is described in this article. For the development of the sensor, an rGO-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocomposite doped thin silica film was deposited over the centrally de-cladded region of a plastic cladding silica (PCS) fiber. In order to get the sensor response, a rigorous experimental investigation was carried out. A linear response from 3% to 70%RH with sensitivity 0.01RH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> (59.1mV/%RH) is observed for the developed sensor. The sensor exhibits an average response and recovery time of 3s & 2.5s, respectively, with a high degree of repeatability.

articleTitle: Coupled Thin Film Dielectric and Gold Layers for High LWIR Emission and Broadband Solar Reflection for Daytime Passive Radiative Cooling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we propose a straightforward thin film-based photonic system to enhance emission at long wave infrared (LWIR) spectrum. The designed structure comprises of thin layers of dielectric material and gold sandwiched on either side of a glass substrate. This configuration demonstrates exceptional LWIR emissivity, nearly reaching 100% and peaking at 9.7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, while also exhibiting remarkable reflectivity of approximately 97% across a broad spectrum from 400 nm to 2200 nm. Furthermore, our proposed design shows a cooling capability of 108 watts per square meter at typical ambient temperatures. The technique can offer a sustainable and green solution for energy-efficient heat management.

articleTitle: A 5T-2C Current-Biased Voltage-Programmed (CBVP) Pixel circuit for AMOLED Displays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, a 5T2C current-biased voltage-programmed (CBVP) pixel circuit is put forth as the backplane technology for AMOLED displays. The designed pixel circuit uses a very low input bias current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{I}_{\text{BIAS}})$</tex> of 0.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> compared to existing designs. It also compensates for the OLED current (IOLED) error for a maximum 1.35 V threshold voltage shift. The maximum emission current error in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{OLED}}$</tex> is 5% for a data voltage of 10 V. Due to low input bias current and compensation for significantly higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}$</tex> shift, the proposed design is suitable for flexible AMOLED displays.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Polarization-Dependent Electro-Optical Switching Studies of Graphene Oxide Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We study the Kerr electro-optic effect, with cross polarizer, in graphene oxide liquid crystal (GOLC) dispersed in water. We obtained a maximum birefringence of around 1.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> mV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> from the concentration-dependent performance of GOLC. In addition to this, we have studied the influence of different polarization states on electro-optical performance in GOLC. Because of its anisotropy, the GOLC shows different Kerr coefficients. Interestingly, we have observed an anomalous behavior in the Kerr coefficient as a function of applied voltage for the different polarization combinations. We have quantified the change in stokes parameters of GOLC under different applied voltages via the circular analyzer method to study the depolarization associated with the cell.

articleTitle: Image Encoding Using Dual Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In recent times, optical data processing has gained significance for efficiently managing vast amounts of data. However, due to sudden explosive growth there is an increasing amount of data traffic that has drawn interest in investigating different parameters of light beams, which can efficiently handle large amounts of data efficiently and securely. This study demonstrated an image encryption technique using an array of vortices that contain orbital angular momentum. The method employs a non-interferometric intensity recording-based encoding, which is easily executable.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Fiber Optic Sensor for Temperature Sensing in Electrical Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and modeling of the two fiber optic sensors (FOS),fiber bragg grating (FBG) sensor and Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) sensor to measure and monitor the temperature changes in electrical substation. Basedon different working principles of sensors the changes in temperatures are determined by observing the changes in bragg wavelength in FBG sensors and Light intensity measurement in MZI sensors. Simulation and analytical methods were carried out to determine and to study the characteristics of the sensors. FOS exclusively has a cutting edge over the otherconventional electrical sensors in terms of Sensitvity values.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Photonic Crystal Based All-Optical OR Gate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The paper proposes a photonic crystal ring resonator (PCRR) based all-optical OR gate. A Y-shaped Junction and a ring resonator are used for designing this gate. The Kerr effect operating on the switching threshold mechanism has been utilized to control how light is coupled into output when a high input intensity is injected into the device. The plane wave expansion method has also been used to determine the operating wavelength, bandgap diagram. The logic inputs of the OR gate have an operating wavelength of 1551.3 nm. The operating power intensity for the proposed OR gate is obtained to be 1 kW/μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the threshold power intensity at 2.8 kW/μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> using the FDTD method. The simulation results are consistent with the logic table of the OR gate, confirming the functionality of the device. The obtained contrast ratio of the structure is 5.73 dB, and the transmission is greater than 0.7. For the designed structure, the response time is 2.33 ps with a fast data rate of 0.43 Tbps which is highly suitable for photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: LASSO-Based Classification of Earthquake Events with Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this manuscript, a dataset collected through Distributed Acoustic Sensors for earthquake event classification is leveraged. The application of the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator model has resulted in an accuracy rate of 99.58%. This performance underscores the advantages of utilizing DAS data, showcasing its potential as a robust and effective tool for earthquake event classification. These findings highlight the promising prospects of DAS technology in seismic monitoring and event classification, offering a valuable contribution to the field of earthquake detection and characterization.

articleTitle: Enhanced Biosensing with Rhombic Ring Resonator in Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals for Proteinuria Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A two-dimensional (2D) Photonic crystal (PC) based biosensor is designed and analyzed for the detection of albumin and urea levels in patients with proteinuria. Ansys Lumericals is a Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) tool used to build rhombic ring resonator structures. With a resonant wavelength of 1546 nm, the maximum obtained values of Quality factor (Qfactor), Full width at half maximum (FWHM), Sensitivity, Figure of Merit (FOM) and Limit of Detection (LOD) are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15,466.5,\ 120\ nm/RIU,\ 0.12nm,\ 1100\ RIU - 1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$54.34\ \times 10 - 6$</tex> RIU respectively. The novelty of this project lies in the combination of 2D photonic crystals, innovative rhombic ring resonator design, highperformance parameters. The achieved values are notably high, which is a novel achievement in the field of biosensing.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Light-Matter Interactions in Platinum Nanoparticles Embedded All-Polymer Microcavity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this study, we highlight how photonic crystal microcavities, recognized for their capability to confine light within small mode volumes, have been utilized to improve the interaction of electromagnetic waves with matter. Specifically, our research showcases the enhanced nonlinear absorption behavior of platinum nanoparticles incorporated between two polymeric Bragg reflectors. The coupling between the light and the nanoparticles leads to a large density of states within the cavity and strong light confinement. Additionally, adjusting the angle of incidence enables the desirable tuning of both the transmittance mode's intensity and its peak wavelength. These results find applications in tunable narrowband optical filters and various optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Accurate Characterization of Optical Phase Modulators Using an Interferometer-Free Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we propose a simple method for the accurate characterization of an optical phase modulator. A GHz-class radio frequency source is used to drive the phase modulator and its output is observed on an optical spectrum analyser (OSA). The relative power levels of the first and second order side bands with respect to the optical carrier, measured from the OSA is plotted as a function of the input RF power. These results are compared with the values expected through simulations, the details of which are discussed in the paper. Simulations are repeated for different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\pi}$</tex> values of the modulator and the specific value that results in the minimum error between the simulated and experimental data points are used to characterise the modulator. This method can be extended to further measure the electro-optic bandwidth of the modulator.

Author Keywords: Carrier to side band power ratio

articleTitle: Picosecond Laser Ablated Si Nanoparticles and Nanostructures for Photonics and SERS Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Silicon is an extensively studied material for its basic properties and device applications in diverse fields including semiconductor devices, solar cells, quantum optics, and biological cells. It is a low-cost and abundant material; hence, different forms including nano-entities of Si are extensively being explored. In the present study, Si nanostructures (NSs) and nanoparticles (NPs) were fabricated in a single trial using a picosecond laser ablation technique (E ∼5 mJ, λ ∼1064 nm, τ ∼30 ps, and at a repetition rate of 10 Hz). The experiments were performed by varying liquid media surrounding the sample. Its effects on the morphology of the fabricated NSs and NPs were studied in detail. For the produced Si NPs, nonlinear optical (NLO) properties were studied using the standard Z-scan technique and it was found that two-photon absorption was the nonlinear absorption mechanism in the Si NPs obtained in all three liquids. Further, the Si NSs produced were coated with a thin gold film and these were used as surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates for sensing a dye molecule Malachite Green (MG). The Si NSs formed in ethanol have shown a good SERS response when compared to other samples. These samples have shown good enhancements with lower relative standard deviations in the SERS signal. These studies involving the synthesis of both NSs and NPs in a single experiment and subsequently utilizing them for different applications can save time and material. Hence, we believe that these results may be helpful for further studies in this direction to explore various applications.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Metasurface with Hexagonal Nanobumps on Flexible Substrate for Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A plasmonic metasurface with sub-wavelength nanobumps of shallow height arranged in a hexagonal pattern on a polymer surface is studied. The metasurface is fabricated through two-step soft lithography technique using an inexpensive colloidal photonic crystal as master. A gold film of 25 nm thickness is sufficient to excite the plasmon mode, resulting in refractive index sensing with a sensitivity of 633 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of Bi-Metallic SPR Biosensor Using $\text{BaTi}{\mathrm{O}_3}$ for Non-Invasive Glucose Detection via Urine Sample
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This work investigates the impact of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaTi}{\mathrm{O}_3}$</tex> based bimetallic SPR sensor. The findings reveal an observed improvement in sensitivity. This study was conducted to detect the presence of glucose in urine samples of individuals suffering from diabetes (glucose of0.625-10 gm/dL), based on associated refractive indices of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.335 - 1.347$</tex>, respectively. The findings of the research demonstrate that the incorporation of BaTiO 3 layers analyzing 12 nm in thickness leads to a notable enhancement in sensitivity, which results in 383.33 degrees/RIU. Further, this enhancement is about three times more compared to the sensitivity seen in the absence of BaTiO3 layers in the bimetallic SPR sensor.

articleTitle: Refractive Index Sensor for the Detection of Malaria Using an Elliptical Channel-Based Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, a photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based RI biosensor for early detection of malaria in individuals using red blood cell (RBC) variation monitoring is presented. The proposed PCF consist of three layers of hexagonal lattice in which elliptical air holes are used. This PCF contain small vertical elliptical channel on which RBCs samples are present. Because of RI difference between samples of both healthy and malaria-infected human RBCs, the peak wavelength of the infected RBC samples deviates from that of the normal RBC samples. With change in highest wavelength, the projected study supports in the finding of the numerous phases of RBCs infected with malaria, namely the Trophozoite phase, Schizont phase and Ring phase. The calculated wavelength sensitivities of the proposed biosensor are 3157.89nm/RIU, 3103.44nm/RIU and 3571.42nm/RIU in the x-polarized direction and 2631.57nm/RIU, 2758.6nm/RIU and 2857.14nm/RIU in the y-polarized direction for Trophozoite phase, Schizont phase and Ring phase respectively. The detection limit is 0.029 which is maximum for the proposed biosensor. Because of little detection limit and improved sensing performance of the suggested RI biosensor based on PCF make it highly appropriate in diagnosis of malaria infection and biological study.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Dynamics in PDI-NDI-PDI Multichromophoric Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) in organic semiconductor materials delivers the study of ultrafast dynamics occurring in femtosecond range. This enables to understand the path of electron transfer in a donoracceptor system and predict the mechanism of charge transfer interactions. The current work focuses on the electron pathway in perylenediimide-naphthalenediimide-perylenediimide (PDINDI-PDI) multichromophoric system on selective excitation of the one of the chromophoric group.

articleTitle: Optical Demux as an Edge Filter for FBG Strain Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of strain measurement, using Fibre Bragg Grating (FBG) strain sensor and optical demux as edge filter. FBG is a key component in the field of optical fibre sensors, are widely popular due to their inherent advantages, and are reliable transducers in measuring physical parameters such as strain and temperature. We design the strain measurement system using passive fiber-optic components. In this experiment, the reflected spectra of the strain FBG is passed through an edge filter, converts any shift in wavelength to intensity change, offering a low-cost solution. We apply gradually weights ranging from 100g to 2000g on the FBG, as a result the strain on the FBG also increases, which in turn causes the FBG pitch to increase, resulting in Bragg wavelength to shift and the results show that as the weight/load increases, there is a gradual shift in the spectrum measured by optical spectrum analyzer (OSA). Results also depict the gradual increase in the optical power as the corresponding wavelength shift occurs due to the positive slope of the edge filter. The sensitivity reported in this study is an improvement in terms of wavelength shift of 1.158 picometer/gram compared to earlier reported work.

articleTitle: High Switching Efficiency in Contour-Nanobowties on VO2 Coated Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a plasmonic contour-nanobowtie placed on a thin layer of VO2 for switching applications. We have utilized finite difference time domain (FDTD) modelling to determine the reflectance and the wavelength tunability of the contour bowtie for different geometrical parameters. The effect of differing the length of the plasmonic bowtie structure and the effect of the gap between the two bowtie segments on intensity switching ratio (ISR) is also analyzed. These nanobowtie structures can be used for switching at desired wavelength by tuning the geometrical parameters.

articleTitle: Binary Differential Joint Transform Correlator Based Rotation Angle Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Joint transform correlator (JTC) is one of the types of optical correlator that provides multiple applications in the field of correlation pattern recognition (CPR), such as security, authentication, and tacking. Log-polar mapping for distortion-invariant CPR is a well-established technique capable of recognizing patterns. It has the potential toprovide information about in-plane rotations. This paper proposes a novel approach of determining angle of in-plane rotation using log-polar mapped binary differential joint transform correlator (BDJTC). Binarization and differential operation have been applied to the recorded intensity distribution, called joint power spectrum (JPS) for having better performance in the logarithmic JTC. Moreover, any change in scale can also be taken care of by the logarithmic mapping, as any scale factor results in a shift in log-polar domain. This approach of rotation-angle determination can benefit numerous fields where faster angle estimation is necessary.

articleTitle: Modulation Characteristics of Ge2Sb2Te5 Metasurface Terahertz Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This study investigates the modulation characteristics of a metasurface incorporating Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> (GST) in the terahertz (THz) frequency range. The transmission spectra of the metasurface in both amorphous (AGST) and crystalline (CGST) phases are analyzed and compared. The results show that the metasurface possesses high contrast in transmission spectra for AGST and CGST at around 1.75 THz. The modulation index was calculated as 96%, indicating the strong potential of the metasurface as a THz switch at this frequency. The mechanism of switching and electric field generation is investigated by analyzing the E-field distribution and current density for both phases. It is found that the high THz conductivity of crystalline GST leads to the absence of field enhancement and wave transmission with a larger value. The findings of this study provide useful insights into the design and optimization of THz devices based on GST metasurfaces.

articleTitle: All-Fiber 2D MMI Based Optical Logic Gates Using Square Core Multimode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a design for implementing various optical logic gates using square-core multimode fiber. We show that NOT/OR/NAND/Ex-OR/Ex-NOR logic operations can be achieved with the same design by manipulating only the phase of input signals.

articleTitle: All Fiber-Optic Ammonia Gas Sensor Using Few-Layer $\text{MoS}_{2}$ Coated Side Polished Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrated the Molybdenum Disulfide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{MoS}_{2})$</tex> based optical ammonia sensor for environmental monitoring and prevention of industrial hazards. This type of sensors are developed by incorporate the layer form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MoS}_{2}$</tex> on a SPF and analyzing the capability of ammonia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{NH}_{3})$</tex> gas sensor. The proposed NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> sensor was works at the humidity level from 60 to 80 % and ambience condition for various gas concentrations from 0 to 490 ppm. The results show an ultra-sensitivity of 86 %, a rapid response time of 21 s, and a fast recovery time of 60 s. Hence, the developed sensor will be a suitable candidate for hazardous ammonia gas detection in the high traffic and industrial fields.

articleTitle: Measurement of Longitudinal Strain Impact on the Signal Group Velocity in PM Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The polarization of light can serve as the fundamen-tal concept for fiber optic sensors. In our earlier publications, we discussed the examination of the correlation between the signal differential group delay in the slow and fast axes of a birefringent optical fiber and the longitudinal tension. We encountered some surprising findings, which we aim to investigate and clarify in this paper.

articleTitle: Fast and Efficient Wavefront Estimation Algorithm Using Slope Values in Zonal Wavefront Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper introduces an approach for zonal wave-front reconstruction based on slope values while improving the wavefront reconstruction time. Wavefront reconstruction from slope values measurement is essential for obtaining accurate and detailed information on a propagating wave. However, Wavefront reconstruction algorithms have several applications in various fields, particularly optics and imaging systems, to restore or analyze wavefront information from the experimental data. This paper investigates the accuracy of the estimated phases at the peripheral grid points where slope information is unavailable, and it improves the computational elapsed time from 0.118 s to 0.101 s. The proposed method involves adapting the Southwell geometry, and the evaluation of wavefront reconstruction performance is conducted by measuring the mean squared error between the applied and reconstructed wavefront.

articleTitle: Stable Detection of Ionized Air by a Highly Excited Raman Silicon Nanocavity Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate the detection of ionized air molecules by a CMOS-fabricated Raman silicon nanocavity laser. The response of the Raman laser emission to negatively ionized air is investigated while changing the excitation power for the Raman laser. It is found that the stability of the detection improves at high excitation powers.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Metamaterial Absorber at Optical Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Numerical studies on a graphene-based metamaterial absorber operating at optical frequencies are presented. The metamaterial absorber consists of one-dimensional gold grating with a disk array in groves on a single layer of graphene supported by a glass substrate. Computer Simulation Technology Microwave Studio is employed for simulations and to get inside the underlying mechanism of absorption in the system.
