The absorber shows an absorption band with almost unity absorptance at wavelength 766 nm. The absorption occurs due to the simultaneous excitation of localised and propagating surface plasmons under the transverse electric (electric field aligns with the length of the grating ridge) mode excitation in the system. The absorber can be exploited in numerous applications, including filters, sensors, thermal emitters, solar cells, and imaging equipment.

articleTitle: Enhanced Nonlinear Optical Properties of ZnS with Carbon Encapsulated Core-shell Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this study, we investigated the enhanced absorptive nonlinearity and optical limiting behaviour of Zinc Sulfide (ZnS) nanoparticles with graphite core-shell structure. The ZnS@C core-shell nanostructures were prepared by nanosecond Pulsed Laser Ablation in Liquid technique. A distinct absorption peak at 288 nm confirms the presence of a graphite layer around the ZnS nanoparticles and the small shift towards longer wavelengths (redshift) in the absorption peak and the changes in the UV absorption band in the ZnS@C core-shell nanostructures, when contrasted with the spectrum of pure ZnS, strongly suggest that electronic interactions are occurring between the ZnS nanoparticles and graphite in their ground states. The nonlinear optical properties of the core-shell nanostructure are investigated with the open aperture Z-scan.

articleTitle: Photonic Generation of 0.1 THz - 0.15 THz Band Based on Train of Radio Frequency Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Photonic assisted system for generation of terahertz signals is proposed and analyzed. Terahertz signals in the frequency range of 0.1 THz - 0.15 THz with a spacing of 0.05 THz are obtained. Depending upon the number of channels, frequency of each channel and frequency spacing between the channels of the train of radio frequency signal generator, terahertz signals in the range of 0.1 THz - 0.15 THz are obtained with distinct power levels for each of the THz frequency component. These terahertz signals can be best suitable for short-range wireless communications for beyond 5G and 6G applications.

articleTitle: Spectral Response of Fiber Bragg Grating Sensor for Contact Microphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) based contact microphone system for tone recognition has been demonstrated in this work. FBG sensor when attached to the surface of an audio device, picks up mechanical vibrations generated by the sound produced. The captured vibrations were converted into shifts in the Bragg wavelength, enabling the extraction of spectral information. A non linear spectral response has been observed by the analysis of magnitude spectrum in the range of 100–1000 Hz. A volume-amplitude analysis was also performed to understand the acoustic detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Phase Modulated Photonic-Crystal Based Gas Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The uncontrolled pollution changes in climate lead to many harmful consequences leading to degradation of mankind along with its surroundings for which a photonic-crystal optical gas detector has been proposed. Phase-change material (PCM) is incorporated to modulate sensing properties. Using geometrical and dimensional optimization, multi-gas detection process has been modeled in range of 650nm to 2500nm and corresponding sensitivities are analyzed. Selectivity of detector to gases such as CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CO in terms of percentage response has been modulated from 12% to 41 % for phase change from amorphous to crystalline or vice-versa.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Metamaterial: Polarization-Insensitive, Highly-Absorptive, and Controllable Thermal Emission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A polarization and angle of incidence insensitive metamaterial perfect absorber has been demonstrated at Infrared wavelengths. This absorber consists of a top layer featuring a grid of Aluminium micro-patches arranged in a square lattice pattern. There is an Aluminium ground plane at the bottom separated by a dielectric layer of Zinc Sulphide. We have fabricated this Metamaterial absorber using UV-lithography followed by lift-off method, and have characterized by angle-resolved infra-red spectroscopy. The metamaterial absorber showed two highly absorptive peaks at 4.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> and at 14.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. Thermal images showed that this metamaterial cab be used as efficient thermal emitters, especially at the Mid Wave Infra-red (MWIR) wavelengths. This kind of structure has the potential applications in precisely controlling thermal radiation.

articleTitle: Luminescent pyrene coupled PMMA microcavities for sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Pyrene microcrystals have been recrystallized using a surfactant. The fluorescence of synthesized microcrystals show the presence of monomer alongwith the red-shifted excimer. The photoluminescence of pyrene microcrystals embedded in microcavities shows whispering gallery modes (WGMs). The sensitivity of these modes towards size and refractive index of the microcavities has been studied. Besides, a theoretical investigation on Purcell effect is presented.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Superior Thermal Sensitivity FBG-Based Temperature Sensor with Metallic and Polymeric Coatings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This research work models and simulates a coated Fibre Bragg Grating (FBG)-based temperature sensor over a range of low to high temperatures. The heat sensitivity of bare FBG is found to be extremely low, making it ineffective for usage in labs or in enterprises. The sensor's cladding is coated with various materials to increase sensitivity. When they were being made, metal coatings revealed their intricacy. To identify an effective coating material for increased thermal sensitivity in both low and high temperatures, this study compares polymeric coating made PDMS with metallic gold coating. In comparison with respect to Bare FBG, which has a sensitivity of 13.33 µK-1, With a sensitivity of 49.33 µK-1, PDMS protected FBG sensors possess the most impressive values.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Mode Control in Fiber Laser Ring Cavity Using Saturable Absorption in Erbium-Doped Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Erbium-doped fiber ring laser with meters-long active fiber will have thousands of longitudinal modes in its lasing peak, which is not desirable for some applications. We present a way to suppress the number of modes by including an unpumped section of erbium-doped fiber which acts as a saturable absorber, and reduces the linewidth of the laser spectrum. We compare two positions for inserting this unpumped fiber into the cavity for controlling the number of modes.

articleTitle: Electronic and Optical Properties of 2D Ferromagnetic CrSiTe3
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Due to its distinctive qualities and potential uses in electronic and optoelectronic devices, the electronic and optical properties of CrSiTe3, a promising two-dimensional (2D) material, have attracted considerable attention. CrSiTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> belongs to the family of transition metal trichalcogenides (TMTCs) and possesses a layered crystal structure, comprising covalently bonded layers of chromium, silicon, and tellurium atoms. The material's absorption and reflectance spectra demonstrate strong polarization dependence and thickness-dependent optical transitions. This unique behavior has ramifications for the development of new optoelectronic devices such as solar cells, Photodetectors and modulators, that can exploit the tunable optical properties of CrSiTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The band structure, partial density of states (PDOS), real and imaginary part of dielectric function, absorption coefficient, of CrSiTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were calculated by using First principle based on density functional theory. CrSiTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is an intriguing topic for research in the area of 2-dimensional materials due to its electrical and optical characteristics. Its tunable band gaps, strong spin-orbit coupling, and unique optical behaviour open up avenues for applications in next-generation optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Pressure Sensor Utilizing a 2D Photonic Crystal Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This research article introduces a pressure sensor design that incorporates a two-domains Photonic Crystal (2DPhCs) - based waveguide structure coupled with nanocavities on both sides, aimed at external pressure detection in the wavelength range of 1591.4 nm to 1601.5 nm. The sensors operational principle hinges on the linear relationship between the resonance wavelength shift and the applied external pressure. The photonic band structure of the designed crystal is assessed via the Plane Wave Expansion (PWE) method, while various sensing parameters are simulated using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method to numerically solve time-dependent Maxwell-equations, effectively modeling electromagnetic wave interactions within the specified propagation domain. The Remarkably, the pressure sensor exhibits a maximum quality factor of 16887, a peak pressure sensitivity (Sp) of 15 nm/GPa, a maximum refractive index sensitivity (SRI) of 365.85 nm/RIU, and an output power exceeding 89% in all cases. The proposed sensor demonstrates strong potential for future fabrication, positioning it as a promising choice for pressure-sensing applications.

articleTitle: A Bow-Tie Shape Dipole Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton for 5/5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This work proposes a compact, wide-band bow-tie shape dipole antenna using spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) for WLAN applications. The proposed antenna comprises an SSPPs-based transmission line (TL) and a bow-tie-shaped radiator. The SSPPs TL acts as a balun to feed the radiator. The bow-tie-like radiator has been used to protract the operating bandwidth of the antenna over the printed dipole radiator. The designed antenna covers the operating bandwidth from 5 to 6.45 GHz (including the WLAN band) with an average realized gain of around 2 dBi and radiation efficiency above 90%.

articleTitle: Spectral Filtering Induced Instability in an All-Fiber Mode-Locked Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this manuscript, we are reporting a state transition in a mode-locked fiber laser operating in dispersion managed regime. The laser is mode-locked by using a semiconductor saturable absorbing mirror (SESAM) and the dispersion management is done by utilizing a chirped fiber Bragg grating (CFBG) which also acts as a spectral filter. In stable conditions, the laser delivers sub-hundred picosecond pulses with a steep-edged spectrum at 17.5 MHz repetition rate. With the increment of the pump power, the spectral width increases, and at a certain pump power when the spectral width is comparable to the FWHM of the spectral filter, the laser transits to a chaotic state. The new state contains a significant amount of temporal instability and shows a smooth trapezoidal-shaped spectrum. The roundtrip-to-roundtrip spectral instability has been characterized by performing dispersive Fourier transform (DFT). A comparative study of relative intensity noise (RIN) between two states has also been performed. This detailed investigation of the chaotic state will surely enrich the study of the pulse dynamics of any mode-locked laser.

articleTitle: Correction of Short Focused Virtual Imaging Systems for Clear Symbology View
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Many optical systems requires imagery to be focused into infinite for clear symbology view. Such applications are Holographic Sight, Head Up Display for Automotives/Military and Augmented reality Head Worn Displays. These are niche products which are very critical in terms of design, material and environment. In this work we will take examples of Head Up Displays and AR Head Worn Displays. Conventional Head Up Displays (HUD) is proven technology in the field of critical data display for operator in airborne as well as automotive application with far field projection. In this paper, a modern and improvised technology called waveguide aided low profile display aid for the purpose of transferring critical information to the operator's eyebox with infinite projection has been discussed. It can be a game changer by reducing weight and size significantly and also able to increase total FOV, eyebox and better forward projection at infinity. A waveguide-based head up display designed and simulated in Zemax opticstudio® has been presented with clear understanding of the infinity projection and correction.

articleTitle: Effect of AlGaN/ AlInGaN Super-Lattice Based Periodically Altered Carrier Injection Layers for UV-C LEDs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the presented manuscript, we report on the theoretical design and analysis of periodically altered super- lattice alloy-based UV-C Light Emitting Diode (LED) with a specifically developed carrier injection layer. The results show that the intermittently fluctuating strained AlGaN/AlInGaN carrier injection region UV-C LED has better performance over its conventional configuration counterpart due to the enhancement in hole transportation, electron overflow suppression, the reduced polarization effect in quantum wells. By ∼106%, the proposed structure outperforms the traditional design in terms of IQE, according to numerical simulations. The electron potential stature has also enlarged from 263 meV to 451 meV, while the hole potential stature has shortened from 321 meV to 270 meV at 200A-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. The superior electron and hole inoculation in the active area is encouraged by the lowered hole barrier height and increased electron barrier height, which is essential for efficient radiative recombination in the diode.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Gratings based Structural Health Monitoring at High Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In order to assure the safety of equipment, temperature and strain monitoring is a crucial responsibility in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) in aircraft structures. High-sensitivity and high-reliability sensors are needed to deliver precise temperature information in real-time. Although bare Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBG) are delicate, direct-write FBG fiber optic sensors have good temperature sensitivity and resistance. By inscribing the sensor in metal tubes, the ability of the sensor for the temperature sensitivity will be increased by two times compared to bare FBG. In- order to illustrate this, in this work we present experimental evaluation of FBG sensor inscribed in the in two different materials namely copper tube and stainless-steel tube, for the evaluation of the strain at the higher temperatures up to 200°C and it's validated with the analog sensors, in addition to this detailed analysis of variation of strain with temperature is also carried using various automation techniques like correlation matrix.

articleTitle: Optimization and Analysis of a Palladium-Coated Tapered Optical Fiber-Based Hydrogen Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This study presents a hydrogen sensor design and simulation using optical fiber and COMSOL Multiphysics. The sensor consists of a palladium-coated tapered optical fiber that transforms upon detecting hydrogen, altering optical properties linked to hydrogen concentration. Simulations show the sensor's response varies with light wavelength, adjustable via parameters like taper diameter and interaction length. Notably, the sensor is highly sensitive, detecting even low hydrogen levels (<4%) with noticeable transmission shifts. It's easily evaluated using LED and photodetector, highlighting its potential for hydrogen detection in energy storage contexts.

articleTitle: A Metal-DBR Interface Structure-Based Tamm Plasmon Sensor for Refractive Index Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this article, we have proposed a Tamm plasmon based sensor for refractive index sensing applications. The suggested framework constitutes of a thin metallic layer followed by 1-Dimensional DBR. We have used Copper (Cu) as the metal layer whereas the DBR structure comprised of Lithium Niobate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{LiNbO}_{3})$</tex> and Silicon dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SiO}_{2})$</tex> as high index and low index layers respectively. For sensing purpose, an ambient medium of refractive index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{a}}=1)$</tex> has been introduced in between the Cu metal and DBR which has been used as a sensing region. When the ambient medium replaced with analytes of interest, a change in output spectrum of the proposed structure has been observed. The DBR of the proposed structure shows a broadband reflection from 504nm to 685nm. When Cu is placed at the front face of DBR, which results in a dip in the reflectivity at 658nm. From the designed structure we attained the maximum sensitivity of 391.28 nm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{RIU}^{-1}$</tex>. Thus, the proposed structure can be used in gas and biosensing applications.

articleTitle: Photonics Based ESM Receiver for EW Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A photonics based ESM receiver for electronic warfare applications is designed and experimentally demonstrated. This system takes the advantage offered by photonics technology by exploiting a direct down conversion architecture for real-time spectrum analysis. The proposed system is a widely tunable coherent optical I/Q receiver with a single stage downconversion of signals from 0.5GHz to 18.5GHz with 1GHz instantaneous bandwidth. In addition an optical frequency comb generator and optical injection locking is designed and developed for a critical phase locking operation to reduce the phase noise of the system. Further improvements are explored, to upgrade the operational bandwidth up to 40GHz.

articleTitle: Key Parameter Measurements & Characterization Methodology for Single Photon Avalanche Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A Single Photon Avalanche Detector (SPAD) is a solid state photodetector which can detect single photons from short duration trigger pulses that can be counted. A major drive into Single Photon Detectors is the explosive growth of quantuminformation science. SPAD systems are most widely used in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems, Geiger mode LIDAR, 3D-Camera, High resolution OTDR, Fluorescence Microscopy and Spectroscopy and Time correlated Single Photon Counting. The development of single-photon detectors is crucial to the advancement of quantum information technologies and measurement science. Detecting single photons is challenging as it's a relatively simple matter to turn a single particle of light into a machine-readable signal. As SPAD is often employed with complex circuitry, the characterization of a detector's properties is necessary. Desired characteristics for detectors include high detection efficiency, low dark count rate, low after-pulsing probability, fast response time, low dead time and low timing jitter. This paper delineates desired characteristics for SPAD for telecom wavelengths, important properties and a method for characterization of SPAD along with simulation results.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Using Adjacently Coupled Semi-Arc Resonator Sandwiched between Pseudo Interdigital Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The paper introduces an innovative strategy of design topology and simulated results for an ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter tailored for modern communication systems. The proposed filter configuration leverages semi-arc resonators sandwiched between pseudo interdigital structure. Operating effectively across the frequency span of 4.3 GHz to 11.1 GHz, the UWB bandpass filter demonstrates an impressive fractional bandwidth of 52.7%. A distinctive feature of this design is its ability to achieve an attenuation of 13 dB, positioned precisely at 7.6 GHz. The presented filter design was implemented using FR-4 as substrate of 1.16 mm thickness with relative permittivity as 4.4. These compelling findings were substantiated through simulations conducted using Keysight Advanced Design System (ADS).

articleTitle: Cavity-Assisted Fluorescence Enhancement of Graphene Quantum Dot Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This article delves into the realm of photonic crystal cavities, engineered to manipulate and enhance fluorescence signals. Photonic crystal cavities effectively confine and amplify emitted light, offering a promising avenue for advancing sensing and imaging technologies. The study details the synthesis of graphene quantum dots using a facile laser irradiation method and the creation of a photonic crystal cavity structure incorporating graphene quantum dots. The resultant structures are characterized, revealing enhanced photoluminescence properties that are better than or on par with reported results. The article explores the principles governing these phenomena and highlights the potential applications in improving fluorescence-based sensing sensitivity and selectivity.

articleTitle: Investigation on Linear Mode Coupling in a Commercial Graded-Index Few Mode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The increasing need for higher data capacity in optical fibers requires exploration of spatial multiplexing techniques, including few-mode and multicore transmission within optical fibers. An essential performance metric to assess is the linear coupling between modes, both before and after implementation. This article delves into a comprehensive numerical analysis of linear mode coupling and the resulting cross talk in a commercial graded index few mode fiber (FMF). We examine how perturbations during fiber fabrication and stress factors during and after deployment impact this coupling. The simulation results presented here mark a significant advancement in enhancing the precision and complexity of models used to describe the transmission of signals in few-mode fibers, with the potential for extending to multicore fibers.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Temporal Dynamics of Quartic Soliton from Low Power Airy Pulse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate the chirp-free quartic soliton shedding from transform limited Airy pulse of peak power 0.2 watt and pulse width of 1 ps. Low power Airy pulse is found efficient in such quartic soliton shedding. In addition, emergent soliton experiences temporal shift towards the leading edge if the pulse power is increased at input. Moreover, the initial chirp parameter makes significant changes to the temporal dynamics of the soliton.

articleTitle: Holographic Defocus Sensor: Astigmatic Lens Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A sensor used to measure the focusing error or the focal plane shift in an optical system can be called a Defocus Sensor. Measurement of focusing error using the Astigmatic Lens approach is a widely used technique due to its simplicity in nature. In this paper, we present a technique for implementing the Astigmatic Lens approach for measuring focusing error using a Computer-Generated Hologram. We present the methodology adopted in this technique along with simulation results.

articleTitle: Total Internal Reflection at the Interface of Lithium Niobate Crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We calculate the phase difference between ordinary and extraordinary polarized wave under total internal reflection for different orientation of optical axis and at different wavelength, and find out the condition for circular polarization in the totally reflected light.

articleTitle: Correlated Color Temperature Estimation Using Digitally Controlled Spectroscopic Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: AS7341 is a multispectral digital sensor used as a spectrometer embedded on a breakout board. It measures the spectral response via eight visible spectrum channels ranging from 350nm to 750nm and two additional channels for clear light and NIR measurement. The device employs an Inter-Integrated Circuit interface for process control and access to data. It was assembled with an open-source microcontroller board to estimate the correlated color temperature of standard display monitors. The device was calibrated using an industrial standard X-Rite color checker chart by measuring the chromaticity coordinates. Upon successful calibration, a few display monitors were analyzed under similar device settings for comparative study. The Correlated Color Temperature (CCT) values obtained using the device from the display screen of Apple's MacBook Air M2 (2022) were found to be the closest resemblance to the predicted values. Further, the CCT range for all devices correlated with the expected CCT range provided by different manufacturers. This experimental design demonstrated that the device can be used for CCT estimation and obtain inferences regarding the intensity and age of various light sources. The small size and portability of the device add to the functionality of the device as an effective spectrometer.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of $Ge_{2}Sb_{2}Te_{5}$ Vertical Photodetector for Silicon Photonic Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present work, the design optimization of vertical photo detector is reported using amorphous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Ge_{2}Sb_{2}Te_{5}$</tex> (a-GST) for silicon platform at telecommunication wavelength 1550 nm. The present work deals with the optimization of both a-GST as well as silicon layers. In the previously reported work, the researchers have optimized the performance only for optimal thickness of a-GST. However, in the present work, the performance of the device is verified for the optimal thickness of the silicon as well as a-GST. It is observed that the photodetector performs better for the lower thickness of the silicon layer for anode contact. However, the silicon thickness can't be reduced after some extent to avoid the metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) design. The results prove the superiority of the proposed design which can be utilized for future device realization.

articleTitle: Nano Photonic Crystal based Sensor for Diabetes Mellitus Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disorder marked by chronically increased levels of blood glucose in persons who are otherwise in good health. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the simulation of photonic crystal based biosensors for diabetes monitoring. The findings indicate that the sensor has the capability to detect glucose concentrations as low as 7 mM (0.13%). Additionally, the study reveals that the sensor can accurately quantify resonance shift even for extremely small fluctuations in glucose concentration. Hence, the photonic crystal based sensor has the potential for the monitoring of diabetes. The sensitivity of the sensor is determined to be 282.1304 nm/RIU with a Q factor of 70.56. The findings of this study hold important significance for the design and development of photonic crystals for diabetes monitoring.

articleTitle: A Compact Slotted Ring Optically Transparent Antenna for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This article presents a circularly polarized transparent coplanar waveguide (CPW) antenna designed for X-band applications. The antenna is designed on a clear transparent glass substrate with a thickness of 1 mm, featuring electrical properties such as a dielectric constant of 4.6 and a tangential loss of 0.0036. The antenna occupies overall area of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.633\lambda \times 0.494\lambda(\lambda$</tex> represents wavelength at 8 GHz) which is relatively smaller in the antennas presented in the literature. Notably, this CPW-configured antenna has its ground plane on the same plane as its antenna components. The constructed antenna covers a frequency range of 7.9 GHz to 13 GHz, encompassing the X-band spectrum while maintaining a 10 dB impedance bandwidth. The antenna achieves radiation efficiency of 99.2 % with realized gain up to 3.2 dBi over the desired band of operation. Additionally, the antenna exhibits circular polarization which supports both left hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand polarization (RHCP) and also ensures that signal quality on both transmission and reception. The outcomes of the proposed transparent antenna shows that the designed antenna could be viable candidate for X-band applications.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Optimization of Lead Free CH3NH3SnI3 Perovskite Solar Cell by Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A high-efficiency organic-inorganic hybrid device opens a new era for accomplishing clean energy. This paper demonstrated the fabrication of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin-film (TF) over CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (lead-free) TF hybrid device for solar cell application using the SCAP-1D numerical simulator. The thickness of the TiO2 TF and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> TF was optimized to be 200 nm and 700 nm, respectively. The experimental optical absorptions of the individual materials were incorporated with the device parameters. High photosensitivity was reported for the device at zero bias under AM 1.5G illumination (300 to 900 nm) condition. Moreover, a high carrier generation rate with enhanced electron current density was observed for the solar device. Simulated device parameters like efficiency, open-circuit voltage, short circuit current density, and fill-factor were found to be 19.29 %, 0.854 V, 27.21 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 82.9 % respectively. In addition, the impact of the device parameters concerning temperature was also studied. The simulated result showed that with increase in temperature, the performance parameters of the device were reduced due to the deformation of interfacial layers and decreasing the mean free path of carriers with temperature.

articleTitle: Advancing Super-Resolution Imaging: A Comprehensive Analysis of Gaussian Fitting in STORM Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Stochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (STORM) has revolutionized our ability to image biological structures and processes at a resolution beyond the diffraction limit of light. Super-resolution is achieved in STORM by accurately localizing the fluorophore dyes attached to the sample. However, image reconstruction in STORM presents significant challenges due to the stochastic nature of the imaging process and the need to localize individual fluorescent dyes accurately. This work presents a detailed analysis of the Gaussian fitting method and its application in STORM microscopy. We discuss the underlying principles of Gaussian fitting, its advantages and limitations, and factors affecting its accuracy. We also provide examples of its successful application in various biological imaging studies. Finally, we highlight the challenges and future directions in fluorophore localization in STORM.

articleTitle: Generating Multiple Polarization Singularities Through Non-Interferometric Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a non-interferometric method for generation of multiple polarization singularities within laser light. Polarization singularities such as V-point and C-point are realized using dualpass modulation approach. The experimental set-up utilizes a pair of identical spatial light modulators for the generation of 7 × 7 array of polarization singularities.

articleTitle: Effective Medium Theory Approach for Sensitive Explosives Characterization in Reflection Mode Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Characterizing highly sensitive explosives can be challenging and dangerous due to their sensitivity to grinding during pellet making, especially for reflection mode THz-TDS configuration. We have employed the Effective medium theory (EMT) approach to address this issue. In this approach, we make a pellet by mixing the Explosive with a binder matrix. Extract the properties of Explosive from composite and binder matrix properties. In the present study, we characterize the premium explosives such as RDX and HMX in the Teflon matrix. Maxwell Garnet, a binary mixture equation, has been utilized to extract the properties of RDX and HMX from the Teflon (binder) and explosive composite mixture.

articleTitle: Effect of the Substrate on the Ultrafast Study of Bismuth Telluride (Bi2Te3)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: To understand the effect of Glass substrate and GaN substrate on Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> material, the ultrafast spectroscopic study was performed in the visible range. The outcome gives information about the energy levels, charge transfer, surface states, and carrier relaxation processes. In GaN/Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Heterojunction the larger amplitude of transient absorption spectra reveals that charge carriers are stabilized in exited energy states due to interface interaction in GaN and Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Our results can be beneficial for the further study of the Bi2Te3/substrate interface, which could be a significant step for the fabrication and designing of nanoelectronics devices having lossless electron transport

articleTitle: Silicon Subwavelength Grating Micro Ring Resonator Refractive Index Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Silicon subwavelength grating microring resonator (SWGMRR) refractive index sensor is proposed for detecting cancer cells. The proposed structure is composed of small silicon bricks with an air gap between them confined in the parameter of straight and ring waveguide of microring resonator all pass system. The proposed structure is simulated around the C band wavelength range using the FDTD method. The SWGMRR is able to detect normal and jurkat cancer cell due to the shift in resonant wavelength of the mode with the sensitivity of 1012 nm/RIU and quality factor of 1219. The proposed device produces sensitivity six times better than the strip waveguide ring resonator simulated at similar dimensions. The proposed SWGMRR exhibits great potential for the quick detection of bioanalytes with much higher sensitivity compared to similar optical resonator-based biosensors.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency in Broadside Coupled Toroidal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The terahertz range of frequencies has in recent times seen significant attention because of the strategic advantages and applications that the frequency range offers. The efficient harnessing of the terahertz range has been possible via the use of artificial materials, or metamaterials. The toroidal excitation is a specific type of electromagnetic excitation which has been explored via carefully designed metamaterials. This study reports the excitation of a single-band electromagnetically induced transparency window via the coupling between two toroidal terahertz metasurfaces in a broadside coupled terahertz metamaterial configuration. The transparency effect is elaborated via electric field profiles and the toroidal excitation in the metamaterial is explained through surface current profile. The broadside coupled toroidal metamaterials provides an added flexibility in modulating the inductive coupling between the two layers for various studies. Studies on meta-modulators, slow light devices, buffers, and other related fields of study can benefit greatly from the terahertz toroidal metamaterials.

articleTitle: Study of Topological Insulator Bi2Se3/GaN and Bi2Se3/Si Heterostructure for Photodetector Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The study of photodetectors with broadband response and strong responsivity-detectivity is crucial. Topological insulators are particularly promising in the quest for materials with remarkable optoelectronic capabilities in the visible to mid-IR region due to their unique Dirac-like surface states and excellent lightabsorption properties. Herein we report the heterojunction of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/GaN and Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Si named as S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> deposited by the thermal evaporation method for highly responsive optoelectronic devices. The excellent performance of the responsivity and detectivity of both samples S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> revealed the fact that the substrates have a major impact on the photoresponse characteristics.

articleTitle: Gold nanoparticle deposited nylon filter paper as a sensitive SERS platform for trace sensing of enrofloxacin in aqueous medium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman Spectroscopy is a molecular sensing method; in it the Raman bands are enhanced manifold upon recording the Raman bands near the vicinity of metal nanostructured surface. The current work reports the fabrication of a low-cost SERS substrate which has been prepared through deposition of gold nanoparticle (AuNP)s over a nylon filter paper (NFP). The AuNPs present in the pores of the filter paper generates electromagnetic hotspot regions which enhance the Raman signals of the analyte. The NFP SERS substrate was first tested with a non-fluorescent dye - 1,2 - bis(4- pyridyl) ethylene (BPE). After testing with the standard Raman probes, the applicability of the fabricated SERS platform is realised through trace detection of a commonly used antibiotic enrofloxacin (ENX).

articleTitle: Design of Laser Diode Driver for High Power Narrow-Line Width Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper the critical parameters of diode driver which affects the amplifier stage in tandem pumped MOPA (Master Oscillator Power Amplifier) configuration are derived and a design is proposed to cater these parameters. This architecture is used to develop diode driver hardware for 1KW, 15GHz line-width LASER amplifier and the experimental result for the same is presented.

articleTitle: Topological Protected Edge State with Ultra-High Q-Factor in One Dimensional Photonic Crystal Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Ahstract- The present manuscript introduces and conducts a theoretical study on a one-dimensional topological photonic crystal (1D TPC). It shows a robust resonant state with an ultra-high-quality factor (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Q}-\text{factor} =10^{9}$</tex>) at the edge of the heterostructure. It has many applications in various scientific fields, like photonic and opto-electronic devices etc.

articleTitle: High Extinction Tunable RF Analogues of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency using Brillouin Scattering for Filtering m-QAM Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel approach to realize analogues of electromagnetically induced transmission response in the RF domain, which is also tunable in terms of frequency of operation. The demonstrated filter has been realized using Brillouin scattering and advanced phase engineering. An extinction ratio of 80 dB at a total optical pump power of 13 dBm has been achieved. We transmitted a quadrature amplitude modulated (QAM) signal through the filter and observed the effect on error vector magnitude (EVM).

articleTitle: Subtraction Microscopy Using Aberrated PSFs for Image Contrast Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Subtraction microscopy is an imaging technique that uses the difference between two images obtained with different point spread functions (PSFs) to improve image contrast. In traditional subtraction microscopy, both images are obtained with unaberrated PSFs with different pinhole sizes. In this paper, we subtracted two images constructed with two PSFs, one with an unaberrated PSF and the other using an aberrated PSF. Here we have presented our preliminary simulation results to establish the outcome.

articleTitle: Screening of Sickle Cells Using Intelligent Microscope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) poses a foremost global health challenge, especially in developing countries where misdiagnosis is common. Timely diagnosis and treatment are crucial in preventing its high mortality rates. To enhance diagnosis, we've created an automated SCD screening system utilizing deep learning. Our method involves two networks that enhance low-resolution microscope images and accurately identify sickle cells. In blind tests, we achieved an impressive accuracy of 96.7%. This costeffective, precise microscope stands as a valuable tool for identifying SCD and addressing blood disorders in resource-constrained areas.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Ring Assisted Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Filters in 45nm SOI Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, design of a micro ring resonator assisted Mach-Zehnder interferometer filter, operating at around 1310 nm wavelength, has been reported. The goal of this study is to serve as a building block analysis for developing more complex wavelength filtering and interleaver circuits. The extinction ratio of the ring-assisted Mach-Zehnder interferometer filter can be tailored by controlling the amount of light coupled to each of the interferometer arms. Both simulation and experimental results indicate with good agreement that upto 4 dB improvement in the extinction ratio over that of a standalone micro-ring device is attained for a 7.54 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> ring radius when operated in over coupled regime for a directional coupler based filter with 20 % power coupling factor.

articleTitle: Inverted Rib-Core Chalcogenide Waveguide for Supercontinuum Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present paper, we proposed a theoretical study of an optical waveguide with a core containing a combination of a slab and inverted slope structure. We have numerically computed the effective index (neff), effective area (Aeff), loss and waveguide dispersion of the present structure. Waveguide's core is considered as GeAsSe and cladding as ZnSe. The super continuum generation (SCG) was generated using 4µm wavelength source pumping at 50fs shows a broad supercontinuum spectrum ranging from 2.2 to 11.5µm.

articleTitle: Genetic Optimization Based Enhanced Sensitivity of FBG Based Simultaneous Measurement of Humidity and Strain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This research focuses on the innovative monitoring of humidity and strain through Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors. Leveraging the FBG's inherent sensitivity to strain-induced Bragg wavelength shifts, we introduce a novel approach to simultaneously measure humidity and strain variations. The study establishes theoretical relationships between strain, humidity, and temperature effects on FBG wavelengths. Furthermore, a unique configuration employing polyimide coatings on FBGs is introduced to enhance sensitivity to humidity-induced strain alterations. Experimental validation is conducted through MATLAB simulations. The investigations encompass various conditions, revealing the dynamic interplay between humidity and strain on FBG wavelength shifts. To optimize sensitivity, a genetic algorithm is employed, leading to enhanced accuracy in simultaneous humidity and strain measurements. The study demonstrates a significant enhancement in sensor sensitivity through the application of genetic optimization techniques. Specifically, the average sensitivity change was found to be approximately 20.5%. This improvement underscores the potential of genetic algorithms in optimizing sensor performance, marking a promising advancement in the field of sensor technology.

articleTitle: Luminescence enhancement studies of europium ions by hydroxy napthoic acid molecules in PVA film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present investigation we have conducted thorough study of luminescence enhancement of europium ion in presence of intramolecular hydrogen bonded hydroxyl napthoic acid molecules in polyvinyl alcohol film. Steady state study of luminescence measurement reveals that in case of 3,2 HNA and Eu3+ doped PVA film, fluorescence of Eu3+ emission increases due to energy transfer from ESIPT state of 3,2 HNA. While subsequent sensitization of Eu3+ luminescence takes place via energy transfer from singlet as well as triplet state of 1,2 HNA.
